items.subject: biology
items.question: What are the main classes of biomolecules? Give one function each.
items.reference:
**Carbohydrates:** Energy source (glucose, starch)
**Proteins:** Enzymes and structural components (hemoglobin, collagen)
**Lipids:** Energy storage and membrane structure (fats, phospholipids)
**Nucleic acids:** Genetic information (DNA, RNA)
items.knowledgeNote: Biomolecules are essential for life. Carbohydrates = (CH₂O)n; Proteins = polymers of amino acids.

items.subject: chemistry
items.question: Describe the chemical changes involved in black-and-white photography, from exposure of the photographic plate to fixing of the print. Give balanced equations.
items.reference:
**Step 1 — Preparation of the plate.** A glass or celluloid plate is coated with a gelatin film containing finely divided **silver bromide**, which is pale yellow and light-sensitive.

**Step 2 — Exposure.** Light energy reduces the silver ions to metallic silver, giving a latent image:

$$2\text{AgBr} \xrightarrow{h\nu} 2\text{Ag} + \text{Br}_2$$

**Step 3 — Developing.** The latent image is intensified by an organic reducing agent such as hydroquinone or potassium thiosulphate solution, converting more exposed AgBr into black metallic silver.

**Step 4 — Stopping and fixing.** The film is fixed in a solution of sodium thiosulphate, which dissolves the unexposed silver bromide so that further light no longer affects it. A wash in hypo solution is followed by washing in running water:

$$\text{AgBr} + 2\text{Na}_2\text{S}_2\text{O}_3 \rightarrow \text{Na}_3[\text{Ag(S}_2\text{O}_3)_2] + \text{NaBr}$$

The areas where silver was deposited print as black; the fixed areas print as the white of the paper.
items.knowledgeNote: Light reduces AgBr to silver metal; sodium thiosulphate fixes the print by dissolving unexposed AgBr as a soluble complex.

items.subject: english
items.question:
A student argues in a class debate: 'Mobile phones should be banned in every school. Everybody concentrates better without them, so banning them will improve our study results.'

(i) What assumption is the speaker taking for granted that has not been proved?
(ii) Give one piece of evidence that would **support** this argument and one that would **weaken** it.
(iii) In one sentence, state the main weakness of the reasoning used.
items.reference:
**(i) Assumption:** That mobile phones are the main cause of poor concentration and poor results, and that concentration is the only factor affecting results. The speaker also assumes that a ban is the only possible solution.

**(ii) Supporting evidence:** A study of two comparable schools, one with a full ban and one without, showing a clear fall in phone-related distractions and a rise in average internal assessment marks in the banning school.
- *Weakening evidence:* Schools in several countries removed phones from classrooms but saw **no** improvement in results, and the decline continued; or teachers report that bans simply move phone use to breaks and the corridor.

**(iii) Main weakness:** The argument moves from a plausible correlation to a certainty about cause and effect without testing other causes, so the conclusion is not logically guaranteed by the evidence given.
items.knowledgeNote: Critical thinking separates fact from opinion, exposes hidden assumptions, and weighs supporting and weakening evidence before accepting a conclusion.

items.subject: physics
items.question: Define capacitance. Derive the capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor.
items.reference:
**Capacitance:** C = Q/V — ability to store charge per unit voltage. SI unit: Farad (F).

**Parallel plate capacitor:** Two plates of area A separated by distance d.
E = σ/ε₀ = Q/(Aε₀)
V = Ed = Qd/(Aε₀)
C = Q/V = Q/(Qd/Aε₀) = **ε₀A/d**

With dielectric (εᵣ): C = εᵣε₀A/d
items.knowledgeNote: 1 F is very large. Typical capacitors: pF to mF range. Parallel plate: C = ε₀A/d

items.subject: biology
items.question: Explain the two major patterns of biodiversity — the latitudinal gradient and the species–area relationship.
items.reference:
**Latitudinal gradient:** species diversity decreases from the equator towards the poles. The tropics have more species — for example the Amazon rain forest supports far more species than temperate forests. Explanations advanced: the tropics have been relatively undisturbed for millions of years, so more time for speciation; they have a stable, predictable climate supporting a high carrying capacity; and more solar energy is available.

**Species–area relationship:** within a region, the number of species increases with area but not linearly: **log S = log C + Z log A**, where Z is the slope of the line (0.1–0.2 in small areas, 0.6–1.2 for very large areas such as continents). The rich diversity of the tropics may partly reflect their vast area.
items.knowledgeNote: The species–area curve is used to estimate how many species are lost when a habitat is fragmented — Z ≈ 0.15 means a 90% habitat loss removes about half the species.

items.subject: chemistry
items.question: Explain why phenol is more acidic than ethanol, and compare their reactions with NaOH and NaHCO₃.
items.reference:
In phenol the −OH oxygen is joined to an sp² carbon of the ring, and the phenoxide ion is stabilised by **resonance** (the negative charge delocalises into the ring). In ethanol the ethoxide ion has no such stabilisation and the ethyl group is electron-donating, destabilising the anion.

Hence phenol ionises readily (pKa ≈ 10) while ethanol does not (pKa ≈ 16):

- Phenol dissolves in **NaOH** forming sodium phenoxide; ethanol does not react with NaOH.
- Neither reacts with **NaHCO₃** (phenol is not acidic enough, pKa 10 vs carbonic acid 6.4) — this distinguishes phenol from carboxylic acids, which liberate CO₂.
items.knowledgeNote: Electron-withdrawing substituents such as −NO₂ increase phenol's acidity; the picrate is strong enough to decompose carbonates.

items.subject: english
items.question: Rewrite as directed: (a) They are building a new bridge. (passive) (b) 'I am leaving tomorrow,' she said. (reported speech) (c) If you had studied, you ___ (pass). (complete) (d) He rarely comes late, ___? (question tag) (e) You ___ not smoke here. (modal of prohibition)
items.reference:
(a) **A new bridge is being built.** (present continuous passive: is/are being + past participle)

(b) **She said that she was leaving the next day.** (backshift the tense; change 'tomorrow' → 'the next day')

(c) **would have passed** (third conditional: had + past participle → would have + past participle)

(d) **does he?** (the sentence is negative with 'rarely', so the tag is positive)

(e) **must** — 'You must not smoke here' expresses prohibition (prohibition may also be 'cannot').
items.knowledgeNote: In reported speech, pronouns, tenses and time words all change together — missing any one of the three loses the mark.

items.subject: mathematics
items.question: Solve dy/dx + y/x = x².
items.reference:
This is linear, dy/dx + Py = Q with P = 1/x, Q = x².

Integrating factor IF = e^(∫P dx) = e^(lnx) = x.

Multiplying through: x·dy/dx + y = x³, i.e. d(xy)/dx = x³.

Integrating: xy = x⁴/4 + C, so **y = x³/4 + C/x**.
items.knowledgeNote: The integrating factor always makes the left side collapse into the derivative of (IF × y) — check this before integrating.

items.subject: physics
items.question: Derive the expression for the impedance of a series LCR circuit and state the condition for resonance.
items.reference:
With the same current I through all elements, the phasor sum of the voltages gives

V = √(V_R² + (V_L − V_C)²) = I√(R² + (X_L − X_C)²),

so **Z = √(R² + (ωL − 1/ωC)²)**.

**Resonance** occurs when X_L = X_C, i.e. ω = 1/√(LC); then Z = R (minimum) and the current is maximum, with the circuit purely resistive.
items.knowledgeNote: At resonance the voltage across L and C can greatly exceed the supply voltage (voltage magnification Q = ω₀L/R).

items.subject: biology
items.question: Differentiate between DNA and RNA on the basis of sugar, strands, bases, stability and function.
items.reference:
DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) and RNA (ribonucleic acid) are both nucleic acids made of nucleotides, but they differ as follows:

| Basis | DNA | RNA |
|---|---|---|
| **Sugar** | **Deoxyribose** (one less oxygen) | **Ribose** |
| **Strands** | **Double stranded**, two antiparallel polynucleotide chains held by hydrogen bonds | Usually **single stranded**; folds on itself |
| **Bases** | A, G, C and **T (thymine)**; A = T and G = C (Chargaff's rule) | A, G, C and **U (uracil)** in place of T |
| **Stability** | More **chemically stable** (no 2'–OH group) — ideal for long-term storage of heredity | **Less stable**, is rapidly degraded — suited to short-term information transfer |
| **Location** | Mainly in the **nucleus** (nucleoid in prokaryotes); also in mitochondria and chloroplasts | In the nucleus **and cytoplasm** |
| **Function** | The **genetic material**; stores hereditary information, replicates it and serves as the template for transcription | **mRNA** carries the message to ribosomes, **tRNA** carries amino acids, **rRNA** is a structural part of the ribosome; some RNAs are the genetic material of viruses |

**Extra point:** both are made of a nucleotide = pentose sugar + phosphate + nitrogenous base, and are linked by **3'–5' phosphodiester bonds**.
items.knowledgeNote: DNA has deoxyribose, is double stranded and uses thymine, making it stable; RNA has ribose, is single stranded and uses uracil.

items.subject: chemistry
items.question: Explain why an alloy is usually harder and stronger than the pure metal. Give the composition of brass and explain why it is preferred to pure gold for making ornaments and musical instruments.
items.reference:
**Why alloys are harder.**

1. The atoms of the second metal are larger than those of the host metal, so in the alloy they cannot fit neatly into the regular lattice of the pure metal. The lattice becomes distorted and the layers are prevented from sliding over one another.
2. The solute atoms obstruct the movement of dislocation, so a much greater force is needed for plastic deformation — the alloy becomes harder and stronger but less ductile.
3. Alloying also raises the melting point and increases corrosion resistance.

**Brass** is an alloy of **copper (70–90%) and zinc (10–30%)**.

**Why preferred over pure gold.** Pure gold is extremely soft (very malleable) and scratches easily, and it is very costly. Brass is hard, durable, corrosion-resistant, has a golden shine, and is far cheaper. Hence brass is used for ornaments, buttons, taps and for bells, trumpets and other instruments where hardness and resonance matter.

**Stainless steel**, another common alloy, is iron with about 11% chromium and is used for kitchen utensils because chromium forms a protective oxide layer that resists rusting.
items.knowledgeNote: Alloying distorts the crystal lattice and blocks dislocation movement, increasing hardness, strength and corrosion resistance.

items.subject: english
items.question:
Read the following data collected by a school and answer the questions that follow.

A survey of 400 students compared mobile phone use with exam performance:
- 240 students (60%) used a phone for more than three hours a day. Of these, 110 scored below 40%.
- 160 students (40%) used a phone for less than one hour a day. Of these, 15 scored below 40%.

(i) Which group performed better on average? Support your answer with figures.
(ii) Can we conclude from this data that heavy phone use **causes** poor results? Give two reasons why not.
(iii) Write one question the school should ask next in order to test the argument fairly.
items.reference:
**(i)** The light-user group performed much better. Only about **9%** of light users failed (15 of 160), while about **46%** of heavy users failed (110 of 240) - roughly five times the failure rate.

**(ii)** No. Two reasons:
1. **Correlation is not causation.** The survey shows the two facts occur together, but the direction of influence is unknown; poor students may also use phones more because they study less, or the results may simply reflect an already existing difference.
2. **Other possible causes (third-variable problem).** Sleep hours, home support, previous attainment, tuition, and motivation could explain both phone use and low marks. The data is also self-reported, so the phone-use figures may be inaccurate.

**(iii)** A fair next question would test a possible underlying factor, e.g. 'On an average school night, how many hours do you sleep?' or 'How many hours per week do you study with the phone in another room?'
items.knowledgeNote: Survey data shows association only; to prove cause you must rule out confounding variables and check that the effect is plausible.

items.subject: physics
items.question: A capacitor of capacitance 6 microF is charged to a potential difference of 100 V. Calculate the energy stored in it.
items.reference:
**Step 1 — Given:** $C = 6\times10^{-6}\ \text{F},\ V = 100\ \text{V}$

**Step 2 — Energy stored in a capacitor:**
$$U = \frac{1}{2}CV^2$$

**Step 3 — Substitute:**
$$U = \frac{1}{2} \times (6 \times 10^{-6}) \times (100)^2 = \frac{1}{2} \times 6\times10^{-6} \times 10^4$$
$$U = 3 \times 10^{-2}$$
$$\boxed{U = \mathbf{0.03\ \text{J}} = \mathbf{3.0 \times 10^{-2}\ \text{J}} = 30\ \text{mJ}}$$

**Step 4 — Verification:** Charge stored $Q = CV = 6\times10^{-6}\times100 = 6\times10^{-4}\ \text{C}$, and $U = \tfrac{1}{2}QV = \tfrac{1}{2}\times6\times10^{-4}\times100 = 0.03\ \text{J}$ ✓

**Equivalent forms:** $U = \frac{1}{2}CV^2 = \frac{1}{2}Q^2C = \frac{1}{2}QV$; energy density $= \tfrac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0E^2$.
items.knowledgeNote: Energy stored in a capacitor equals one-half of capacitance times potential difference squared, here 0.03 joules.

items.subject: biology
items.question: Distinguish between in-situ and ex-situ conservation with Nepali examples.
items.reference:
**In-situ conservation** protects species in their natural habitat, where they evolve and interact naturally. Examples: protected areas — Chitwan, Bardia, Sagarmatha, Langtang and Shivapuri Nagarjun national parks, Koshi Tappu Wildlife Reserve (waterbirds), and the Annapurna Conservation Area (community-based, with buffer zones and local participation).

**Ex-situ conservation** protects species outside their habitat, in zoos, botanical gardens, seed banks, cryopreservation or captive-breeding centres — used when a species is critically endangered or its habitat is gone. Examples: the Central Zoo (Jawalakhel) for captive breeding of red panda and gharial, the National Botanical Garden (Godavari) for plants, and the National Agriculture Research Council's gene bank for seed conservation.

In practice the two are complementary: ex-situ populations can be reintroduced (gharial in Chitwan), while in-situ protection maintains the habitat that makes reintroduction possible.
items.knowledgeNote: Nepal's most effective in-situ tool has been the buffer-zone/community-forestry model — local ownership is what reduced poaching of one-horned rhino.

items.subject: chemistry
items.question: Write the reactions of phenol with (a) bromine water, (b) conc. HNO₃ and (c) Zn dust, and explain why phenol is more reactive than benzene towards electrophiles.
items.reference:
**(a)** bromine water gives 2,4,6-tribromophenol (a white precipitate) without a catalyst.

**(b)** conc. HNO₃ gives picric acid (2,4,6-trinitrophenol).

**(c)** Zn dust distils phenol to benzene, removing the OH group.

**Reason:** the −OH group has a strong +R effect, so the ring is activated; the ortho and para positions acquire high electron density, allowing mild electrophiles to attack — benzene needs a Lewis-acid catalyst and gives only mono-substitution.
items.knowledgeNote: The −OH group is ortho/para-directing as well as ring-activating; halogenation in phenol needs no FeBr₃ whereas benzene does.

items.subject: english
items.question: Fill in the blanks with a suitable article, preposition or tense form: (a) She is ___ honest woman. (b) I have been waiting ___ two hours. (c) By the time we arrived, the film ___ (start).
items.reference:
(a) **an** — 'honest' begins with a vowel sound (the h is silent), so the indefinite article is 'an'.

(b) **for** — 'for' precedes a duration (two hours), whereas 'since' marks a point in time (since 2 o'clock).

(c) **had started** — the past perfect expresses an action completed before another past action ('by the time we arrived').
items.knowledgeNote: Test the article by sound, not spelling: 'a university' (y-sound) but 'an umbrella'.

items.subject: mathematics
items.question: Solve the differential equation dy/dx = (1 + y²)/(1 + x²).
items.reference:
The variables separate:

dy/(1 + y²) = dx/(1 + x²).

Integrating both sides: tan⁻¹y = tan⁻¹x + C.

**General solution:** tan⁻¹y − tan⁻¹x = C (equivalently (y − x)/(1 + xy) = tan C after applying the difference formula).
items.knowledgeNote: Recognise the separable form first; standard integrals ∫dx/(1 + x²) = tan⁻¹x are the whole content of the question.

items.question: दिइएका समस्त पदको विग्रह गरी समासको भेद पहिचान गर्नुहोस्: (क) राजपुत्र (ख) नीलकण्ठ (ग) आमाबाबु (घ) मुखचन्द्र।
items.reference:
**(क) राजपुत्र = राजाको पुत्र** — सम्बन्ध षष्ठी (को) र अर्थ परपद 'पुत्र' मा प्रधान → **तत्पुरुष समास**।

**(ख) नीलकण्ठ = नीलो कण्ठ भएको, अर्थात् शिव** — अर्थ तेस्रो (शिव) मा गयो → **बहुव्रीहि समास**।

**(ग) आमाबाबु = आमा र बाबु** — दुवै पद प्रधान → **द्वन्द्व समास**।

**(घ) मुखचन्द्र = चन्द्रजस्तो मुख** — विशेषण-विशेष्य (उपमान-उपमेय) नाता → **कर्मधारय समास**।
items.knowledgeNote: भेद छुट्याउने चाबी प्रधानता हो — अर्थ तेस्रोतिर गयो भने तुरुन्त बहुव्रीहि।

items.subject: physics
items.question: Define root-mean-square value of alternating current. Show that for a sinusoidal current the rms value is 1/√2 times the peak value.
items.reference:
The **rms value** is the steady direct current that would produce the same average heating in a resistor: I_rms = √(mean of I²).

With I = I₀ sin ωt, I² = I₀²sin²ωt = I₀²(1 − cos2ωt)/2. The cosine term averages to zero over a cycle, so mean I² = I₀²/2 and

**I_rms = I₀/√2 ≈ 0.707 I₀**.
items.knowledgeNote: Meters read rms values; a.c. power P = I_rms V_rms cos φ, where cos φ is the power factor.

items.subject: biology
items.question: Describe the structure of a nucleotide and explain its role in DNA.
items.reference:
A **nucleotide** consists of: (1) a pentose sugar (deoxyribose in DNA, ribose in RNA), (2) a nitrogenous base (A,T,G,C in DNA), (3) a phosphate group.

In DNA, nucleotides form a double helix via complementary base pairing (A-T, G-C) connected by hydrogen bonds.
items.knowledgeNote: DNA = deoxyribonucleic acid; RNA = ribonucleic acid. DNA stores genetic info; RNA transfers it.

items.subject: chemistry
items.question: Describe the preparation and setting of plaster of Paris. Give balanced equations and state why it cannot be used as a permanent building material.
items.reference:
**Preparation.** Gypsum is heated in a kiln at about 373 K so that three-fourths of its water of crystallisation is lost:

$$2(\text{CaSO}_4\cdot2\text{H}_2\text{O}) \xrightarrow{373 \ \text{K}} (\text{CaSO}_4)_2\cdot\text{H}_2\text{O} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O}\uparrow$$

The product is **plaster of Paris** (hemihydrate, $(CaSO_4)_2\cdot H_2O$), a white powder.

**Setting.** When mixed with water it absorbs the water again and forms a hard interlocking mass of gypsum:

$$(\text{CaSO}_4)_2\cdot\text{H}_2\text{O} + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow 2(\text{CaSO}_4\cdot2\text{H}_2\text{O})$$

The interlocking crystals expand slightly and bond to the wall.

**Why it is not a permanent material.** The hardened mass is **gypsum** $(CaSO_4\cdot2H_2O)$, not anhydrous calcium sulphate. In the presence of water it dissolves again to form hemihydrate, so the plaster is destroyed by rain or by water leakage. It is therefore used only for interior work, ceiling and false roofs, decorative work, casts and surgical plaster.

**Related reaction.** Gypsum is manufactured from limestone and sulphuric acid:
$$\text{CaCO}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{CaSO}_4\cdot2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CO}_2\uparrow$$
items.knowledgeNote: Plaster of Paris, (CaSO₄)₂·H₂O, sets by absorbing water to form gypsum, so it dissolves again in water and is not permanent.

items.subject: english
items.question: What is critical thinking? Explain any three of its key skills with examples.
items.reference:
**Critical thinking** is disciplined, evidence-based reasoning instead of accepting claims at face value.

**Skills:** (1) **Analysis** — breaking an argument into premises and conclusion. (2) **Evaluation** — testing evidence quality (a viral health claim vs a peer-reviewed trial). (3) **Inference** — drawing warranted conclusions (wet streets → it rained, barring alternatives).
items.knowledgeNote: Bloom's ladder (remember → create) places evaluation and creation at the top — exams increasingly target those rungs.

items.subject: mathematics
items.question: If A = [[2,1],[3,4]], find det(A) and A⁻¹.
items.knowledgeNote: A·A⁻¹ = I (identity matrix). Inverse exists only if det ≠ 0.

items.subject: nepali
items.question: निम्नमध्ये कुन शब्द तत्पुरुष समास हो? (क) मामाचेला (ख) नेपालभाषा (ग) दशलाख (घ) चतुर्दशी
items.reference:
**सही उत्तर: (ख) नेपालभाषा**

'नेपालभाषा' = **नेपाल + भाषा**। यहाँ द्वितीय (अधिलम्बित) पदबाट 'को' विभक्ति विलोप भई **प्रथम पद (नेपाल) मात्र प्रधान** भएकाले यो **तत्पुरुष समास** हो।

अन्य विकल्पहरू:
- **(क) मामाचेला** = मामा + चेला — दुवै पद स्वतन्त्र, अर्थपूर्ण र समान पदा भएकाले **द्वन्द्व समास** हो।
- **(ग) दशलाख** = दश + लाख — अङ्क र अङ्क जोडिएकाले **अङ्कात्मक द्विगु समास** हो।
- **(घ) चतुर्दशी** = चतुः + दशी — यो पनि अङ्क र अङ्क जोडिएकाले **अङ्कात्मक द्विगु समास** हो।
items.knowledgeNote: तत्पुरुष समासमा द्वितीय पदको विभक्ति विलोप भई प्रथम पद मात्र प्रधान हुन्छ, जस्तै नेपालको भाषा = नेपालभाषा।

items.subject: physics
items.question: Define capacitance. Derive the capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor.
items.reference:
**Capacitance** C = Q/V: charge stored per unit voltage. SI unit: **farad (F)**.

Two plates of area A, separation d, charge ±Q: field E = σ/ε₀ = Q/(Aε₀). Potential V = Ed = Qd/(Aε₀).

C = Q/V = **ε₀A/d**. With a dielectric of constant εᵣ filling the gap: C = εᵣε₀A/d.
items.knowledgeNote: 1 F is enormous — real capacitors live in the pF–mF range, so NEB answers in μF/pF are a sanity check.

items.subject: biology
items.question: State the four major causes of biodiversity loss and explain any one in detail.
items.reference:
The **'evil quartet'**:
1. **Habitat loss and fragmentation** (most important) — clearing forests, draining wetlands, building roads, which shrinks and isolates populations.
2. **Over-exploitation** — hunting, fishing and harvesting beyond replacement (rhino/elephant poaching, tiger trade).
3. **Alien (invasive) species** — introduced species outcompete natives, e.g. *Eichhornia* (water hyacinth) clogging water bodies, *Lantana* in forests.
4. **Co-extinction** — when a host or partner species goes extinct, species dependent on it follow (a pollinator with its plant, a parasite with its host).

Habitat loss is the dominant driver because it removes the shelter, food and breeding sites a species needs and also splits one population into small, inbreeding fragments.
items.knowledgeNote: The most recent threat category being tracked globally is over-exploitation of high-value species — the direct link between illegal trade and extinction risk.

items.subject: chemistry
items.question: Give the Williamson synthesis of an ether and explain why it fails for tertiary alkyl halides.
items.reference:
**Williamson synthesis:** sodium alkoxide + primary alkyl halide →

R−ONa + R′X → R−O−R′ + NaX (SN2, best with primary halides).

**Failure with tertiary halides:** the bulky tertiary substrate cannot undergo backside SN2 attack; it ionises to a carbocation that is attacked by the alkoxide as a base, so **elimination (alkene)** dominates instead of substitution.
items.knowledgeNote: For unsymmetrical ethers choose the more hindered group as the alkoxide and the less hindered as the halide.

items.subject: english
items.question: Correct the errors: (a) One of my friend is a doctor. (b) Walking down the road, a snake bit me. (c) She is senior than me.
items.reference:
(a) One of my **friends is** a doctor — 'one of' takes a plural noun but a singular verb.

(b) **Walking down the road, I was bitten by a snake.** The original has a dangling modifier: the participle must describe the subject of the main clause, and 'a snake' cannot be walking.

(c) She is senior **to** me — 'senior', like 'junior', 'superior' and 'inferior', takes 'to', not 'than' (Latin comparatives).
items.knowledgeNote: Dangling modifiers are the classic error-correction item: check that the introductory participle logically belongs to the main subject.

items.subject: mathematics
items.question: Write the order and degree of the differential equation (d²y/dx²)² + (dy/dx)³ = 0.
items.reference:
**Order** = the order of the highest derivative present = **2** (d²y/dx²).

**Degree** = the power of the highest-order derivative when the equation is polynomial in derivatives = **(d²y/dx²)² has power 2**, so degree = 2.

The equation is thus of order 2 and degree 2 (it is not linear, since it contains the square of the second derivative).
items.knowledgeNote: Degree is read only after clearing radicals and fractions in the derivatives — always rewrite in polynomial form before reading it off.

items.subject: nepali
items.question: दिइएका अशुद्ध वाक्य शुद्ध गरी लेख्नुहोस्: (क) उनी आएको छैन। (ख) मैले भोलि जान्छु। (ग) सबै विद्यार्थीहरूले परीक्षा दिए।
items.reference:
**(क)** 'उनी' आदरार्थी भएकाले क्रिया बहुवचनमा — **उनी आएका छैनन्।**

**(ख)** 'मैले' भाववाच्य/कर्मणि प्रयोग हो; कर्तृवाच्यमा — **म भोलि जान्छु।** (यहाँ 'ले' विभक्ति नमिल्ने हुन्छ।)

**(ग)** 'सबै' र 'हरू' दुवै बहुवचन भएकाले एउटा मात्र — **सबै विद्यार्थीले परीक्षा दिए।**

शुद्धीकरण गर्दा विभक्ति, वचन र लिङ्गको मेल जाँच्नु नै मुख्य काम हो।
items.knowledgeNote: आदरार्थी कर्तासँग बहुवचन क्रिया प्रयोग हुन्छ — यो नेपाली व्याकरणको नियमित परीक्षा-बिन्दु हो।

items.subject: physics
items.question: A transformer with 1000 turns in the primary and 100 turns in the secondary is connected to a 220 V a.c. mains. Find the secondary voltage and the secondary current when the primary current is 0.2 A (assume an ideal transformer).
items.reference:
V_s/V_p = N_s/N_p → V_s = 220 × 100/1000 = **22 V**.

For an ideal transformer, V_pI_p = V_sI_s → I_s = (220 × 0.2)/22 = **2 A** — the voltage steps down by 10, so the current steps up by 10.
items.knowledgeNote: A step-down transformer gives lower voltage but higher current; energy conservation (ideal case) requires V_pI_p = V_sI_s.

items.subject: biology
items.question: Explain how temperature and pH affect enzyme activity, and state the advantage of using immobilised enzymes in industry.
items.reference:
**Enzymes** are biological catalysts — mostly proteins — that speed up reactions by lowering the **activation energy** without being used up.

**Effect of temperature**
- As temperature rises, molecules gain kinetic energy and the **rate of reaction increases** up to an **optimum temperature**.
- Above the optimum, the weak bonds maintaining the enzyme's tertiary structure break and the enzyme is **denatured**, so the active site loses its shape and the **rate falls to zero**. The enzyme molecule is not consumed, it is permanently changed.
- Optimum is about **37 °C** for most human enzymes, but the thermophilic bacterium *Thermus aquaticus* gives **Taq DNA polymerase** with an optimum near **72 °C** that stays active at 95 °C — the basis of **PCR**.

**Effect of pH**
- Every enzyme has an **optimum pH** at which the ionisation of the amino acids of its active site is correct for substrate binding.
- **Pepsin** works best at about **pH 2** (stomach), **trypsin** at about **pH 8–9** (small intestine) and **salivary amylase** at about **pH 6.7–7**.
- A shift in pH changes the charges on the active site and on the substrate, so the enzyme–substrate complex fails to form and activity drops; extreme pH also denatures the enzyme.

**Advantage of immobilised enzymes**
- Enzymes are bound to an **insoluble inert support** such as **calcium alginate beads**, DEAE-cellulose or acrylamide gel.
- They can then be **reused many times**, are **more stable** to heat and pH, and the **product can be separated easily** from the enzyme, allowing continuous flow operation and reducing cost — e.g. **lactase** to make lactose-free milk, **glucose isomerase** to convert glucose syrup into fructose syrup, and **urease** in urea-based biogas plants.
items.knowledgeNote: Every enzyme has an optimum temperature and pH; immobilised enzymes are reusable and make product separation easy.

items.subject: chemistry
items.question: Describe the Haber process for ammonia manufacture. Why is high pressure used?
items.reference:
N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ + heat. Conditions: 450–500°C (rate vs yield compromise), **~200 atm**, Fe catalyst with Mo promoter, unreacted gases recycled.

**High pressure** because 4 gas moles → 2: Le Chatelier drives the equilibrium toward NH₃, and pressure also speeds collisions.
items.knowledgeNote: Ammonia feeds fertilisers (urea, ammonium nitrate), explosives, and plastics — the highest-volume synthesis on Earth.

items.subject: english
items.question: Distinguish between fact and opinion with two examples of each.
items.reference:
**Fact** is verifiable: 'Mt. Everest is 8,848.86 m high.' 'Water boils at 100°C at sea level.'

**Opinion** expresses judgement: 'Pokhara is Nepal's most beautiful city.' 'Online classes are better than physical ones.'

Test: can evidence settle it? Yes → fact; no → opinion.
items.knowledgeNote: Editorials blend both — spotting which sentence is which is the core critical-reading move.

items.subject: mathematics
items.question: Solve for $x$: $\quad 2\sqrt{x+1}=x-3$
items.reference:
**Step 1 (arrange):** $x-3=2\sqrt{x+1}$. Since the right side is positive we need $x>3$.

**Step 2 (square both sides):**
$$(x-3)^{2}=4(x+1)$$
$$x^{2}-6x+9=4x+4$$
$$x^{2}-10x+5=0$$

**Step 3 (solve the quadratic):**
$$x=\frac{10\pm\sqrt{100-20}}{2}=\frac{10\pm\sqrt{80}}{2}=\frac{10\pm4\sqrt5}{2}=5\pm2\sqrt5$$

**Step 4 (reject the extraneous root):** $5-2\sqrt5\approx 0.528 < 3$, violating $x>3$. Reject it.

**Verification for $x=5+2\sqrt5$:**
$$\text{LHS}=2\sqrt{6+2\sqrt5}=2\sqrt{(1+\sqrt5)^{2}}=2(1+\sqrt5)=2+2\sqrt5$$
$$\text{RHS}=5+2\sqrt5-3=2+2\sqrt5\quad\checkmark$$

$$\boxed{x=5+2\sqrt5}$$
items.knowledgeNote: Squaring can create false roots — always substitute back; here $x>3$ is forced by $\sqrt{x+1}>0$.

items.question: दिइएका वचनहरूको बहुवचन रूप लेख्नुहोस्: (क) कक्षा (ख) पुस्तक (ग) घर

(ख) पुस्तक → **पुस्तकहरू**

items.subject: physics
items.question: A parallel plate air capacitor has plates of area 0.04 m² separated by 2 mm. Calculate its capacitance. (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² F/m)
items.knowledgeNote: C ∝ A/d — doubling the plate area or halving the gap doubles the capacitance.

items.subject: biology
items.question: What is Bt cotton? Explain how the Bt toxin kills the insect pest.
items.reference:
**Bt cotton** is a transgenic crop carrying **cry genes** from the soil bacterium *Bacillus thuringiensis*, introduced by recombinant DNA technology so that the plant makes its own insecticidal protein.

The introduced gene is expressed as an **inactive protoxin crystal** in the plant. When the insect larva eats the plant tissue, the crystals enter its gut, where the **alkaline pH dissolves them** and converts the protoxin into active toxin. The active toxin binds to the surface of midgut epithelial cells, creating pores; cells swell and lyse, the gut is perforated, the larva stops feeding and dies.

The toxin is harmless to the plant, to humans and to mammals because their gut is acidic and the protoxin is not activated.
items.knowledgeNote: The alkaline-gut requirement is the crucial safety argument — Bt toxin is species specific, not a general poison.

items.subject: chemistry
items.question: Describe the mechanism of nucleophilic addition to a carbonyl group and explain why aldehydes are more reactive than ketones.
items.reference:
The carbonyl carbon is electron-deficient (sp², δ⁺) and the π bond is polarised, so nucleophiles attack the carbon:

(i) Nu⁻ attacks the carbon, the π electrons move to oxygen giving a tetrahedral alkoxide intermediate; (ii) protonation of the alkoxide by the medium completes the addition, giving an alcohol (or a derivative if the nucleophile is followed by loss of water).

**Aldehydes vs ketones:** two alkyl groups in a ketone release electron density by +I effect, reducing the carbon's δ⁺, and their bulk also hinders attack. Hence aldehydes react faster; formaldehyde is the most reactive.
items.knowledgeNote: Acid catalysis helps weak nucleophiles (protonation increases electrophilicity); base catalysis helps strong ones — the intermediate is stabilised.

items.subject: english
items.question:
Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

Forests are often called the lungs of the earth, yet their value is rarely measured in the language of markets. A standing forest prevents landslides, recharges springs, shelters pollinators and stores carbon; a cleared slope yields timber once and then costs the community every monsoon. Nepal's community forestry programme was built on this insight: when the people who live beside a forest manage it, they protect what a distant contractor would remove.

(a) Why is the market value of a forest misleading? (b) State two services a standing forest provides. (c) What was the insight behind community forestry? (d) Find a word in the passage that means 'a person who supplies goods under contract'.
items.reference:
(a) Because markets price only the timber that can be sold, while the forest's real benefits — preventing landslides, recharging springs, sheltering pollinators and storing carbon — are never bought or sold.

(b) Any two: it prevents landslides; it recharges springs; it shelters pollinators; it stores carbon.

(c) That the people who live beside a forest will protect it, whereas a distant contractor removes it for one-time profit.

(d) 'contractor'.
items.knowledgeNote: Comprehension answers must be in your own words and supported by the text; copying whole sentences without answering the point loses marks.

items.subject: mathematics
items.question: Differentiate: (a) y = x³ tan x, (b) y = ln(sinx).
items.reference:
**(a)** product rule: dy/dx = 3x²·tan x + x³·sec²x = **x²(3 tan x + x sec²x)**.

**(b)** chain rule: dy/dx = (1/sinx)·cosx = **cot x** (valid for sinx > 0).

State the rule used for each: product rule for (a), chain rule for (b).
items.knowledgeNote: With more than two factors, differentiate one factor at a time and add the terms — the same rule extends to a triple product.

items.subject: nepali
items.question: 'सामुदायिक वनको महत्त्व' विषयमा आवधिक निबन्ध लेख्नुहोस्।
items.reference:
**भूमिका:** नेपालको वन संरक्षणमा सामुदायिक वन एक सफल अभ्यास हो — जनसहभागिताले वन बचाएको मात्र नभई गाउँको अर्थतन्त्र बदलेको छ।

**विस्तार:**
१. **वातावरणीय महत्त्व:** पहिरो रोकथाम, जलस्रोत संरक्षण, जैविक विविधता र कार्बन भण्डारण।
२. **आर्थिक महत्त्व:** दाउरा, घाँस, काष्ठ र औषधिजन्य वनस्पति; सदस्यको श्रमबाट वन पैदावर आय।
३. **सामाजिक महत्त्व:** महिला र सीमान्तित समुदायको सहभागिता, समूहमा निर्णय, दायित्वको भावना।
४. **चुनौती:** काष्ठको अत्यधिक दोहन, सदस्यबीच विवाद, नेतृत्वको कमजोरी, जलवायु प्रकोप।

**निष्कर्ष:** सामुदायिक वन संरक्षणको साधन र विकासको माध्यम दुवै हो; जनसहभागिता कायम राख्दा नै यसको सफलता दिगो हुनेछ।
items.knowledgeNote: आवधिक निबन्ध भूमिका → बुँदागत विस्तार → निष्कर्ष यही ढाँचामा लेख्नुहोस्; हरेक अनुच्छेदमा एउटा मात्र बुँदा।

items.subject: physics
items.question: What is modulation? Distinguish between amplitude modulation and frequency modulation, and state one advantage of FM over AM.
items.reference:
**Modulation** is the process of superimposing a low-frequency message signal on a high-frequency carrier wave so the signal can be radiated over long distances by an antenna of practical size.

**AM:** the amplitude of the carrier varies with the message; the sideband bandwidth is 2f_m, and noise affects amplitude strongly.

**FM:** the frequency varies with the message; bandwidth ≈ 2(f_m + Δf), which is wider.

**Advantage of FM:** noise immunity — amplitude noise (lightning, sparks) can be clipped away, so reception is much clearer.
items.knowledgeNote: Antenna length must be comparable to λ/4, which is why audio (≈20 Hz–20 kHz) cannot be radiated directly and needs a carrier in the MHz range.

items.subject: biology
items.question: What are the main classes of biomolecules? Give one function of each.
items.reference: **Carbohydrates:** energy source (glucose, starch). **Proteins:** enzymes and structure (haemoglobin, collagen). **Lipids:** energy storage and membranes (fats, phospholipids). **Nucleic acids:** genetic information (DNA, RNA).
items.knowledgeNote: Carbohydrates ≈ (CH₂O)n; proteins are amino-acid polymers — composition formulas both get tested.

items.subject: chemistry
items.question: What is the Contact process? Write the key reactions and conditions.
items.reference:
Manufacture of **sulphuric acid**: (1) S + O₂ → SO₂; (2) 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ (V₂O₅, 450°C, 1–2 atm); (3) SO₃ + H₂SO₄ → H₂S₂O₇ (oleum); (4) H₂S₂O₇ + H₂O → 2H₂SO₄.

SO₃ is absorbed in acid, never water directly (which makes unabsorbable mist).
items.knowledgeNote: 'King of chemicals' — national H₂SO₄ output tracks industrial capacity, an NEB essay staple.

items.subject: english
items.question: What are premises and conclusions in an argument? Identify them in: 'All students must wear uniforms since uniforms reduce economic discrimination.'
items.reference:
**Premises** are the supporting reasons; the **conclusion** is the claim they support (flagged by 'therefore, so, since, because').

**Premise:** 'uniforms reduce economic discrimination.' **Conclusion:** 'All students must wear uniforms.'

Critical check: does the premise really entail the conclusion, or are cheaper alternatives (dress codes, subsidies) ignored?
items.knowledgeNote: 'Since/because' introduce premises; 'therefore/so' introduce conclusions — indicator words map arguments instantly.

items.subject: mathematics
items.question: Prove: A ∪ (B ∩ C) = (A ∪ B) ∩ (A ∪ C) (distributive law of sets).
items.reference:
LHS: x ∈ A ∪ (B ∩ C)
⇔ x ∈ A or (x ∈ B and x ∈ C)

RHS: x ∈ (A ∪ B) ∩ (A ∪ C)
⇔ (x ∈ A or x ∈ B) and (x ∈ A or x ∈ C)

Using distributive law of logic: P or (Q and R) = (P or Q) and (P or R)
∴ LHS = RHS. Proved.
items.knowledgeNote: De Morgan's laws: (A∪B)' = A'∩B' and (A∩B)' = A'∪B'

items.subject: nepali
items.question: निम्न शब्दहरूमा उपसर्ग छुट्याई उपसर्गको नाम र शब्दको अर्थ लेख्नुहोस्: (१) प्रभार (२) प्रवास (३) अभय (४) सगति।
items.reference:
(१) **प्रभार = प्र + भार** — उपसर्ग **'प्र'**; अर्थ — प्रतिभार गर्नु, थिच्नु; सामाजिक दबाब।
(२) **प्रवास = प्र + वास** — उपसर्ग **'प्र'**; अर्थ — परिवास गर्नु (बस्नु), अर्को देशमा बस्नु।
(३) **अभय = अ + भय** — उपसर्ग **'अ'**; अर्थ — निर्भय रहनु, सुरक्षित हुनु।
(४) **सगति = स + गति** — उपसर्ग **'स'**; अर्थ — सहगति गर्नु, साथ दिनु।

यी चारै शब्दमा उपसर्ग मूल शब्दको अर्थलाई बदलेर शब्दमा नयाँ अर्थ दिएको छ।
items.knowledgeNote: उपसर्ग मूल शब्दको अर्थ बदल्ने शब्द-प्रयोगी तत्व हो, जस्तै 'अ + भय = अभय' भने निर्भय हुनु।

items.subject: physics
items.question: Capacitors of 2 μF and 3 μF are connected (i) in series and (ii) in parallel. Find the equivalent capacitance in each case.
items.reference:
(i) Series: 1/C = 1/2 + 1/3 = 5/6 → C = **1.2 μF** (series is always smaller than the smallest).

(ii) Parallel: C = 2 + 3 = **5 μF**.
items.knowledgeNote: Capacitors combine oppositely to resistors: series shrinks, parallel adds — mixing them up is the standard trap.

items.subject: biology
items.question: What is gene therapy? Describe its use in ADA deficiency with the steps of the first clinical procedure.
items.reference:
**Gene therapy** is the correction of a genetic defect by introducing a normal functional gene into a person's cells or tissues.

**ADA deficiency** (adenosine deaminase deficiency) causes severe combined immunodeficiency: without the enzyme, deoxyadenosine accumulates and destroys lymphocytes, so the child has no immune defence.

**Procedure:** lymphocytes are taken from the patient's blood, a functional ADA cDNA is introduced with a retroviral vector, and the corrected cells are returned to the patient. The lymphocytes have a limited life, so the treatment must be **repeated periodically**. A permanent cure requires the gene to be introduced into bone-marrow stem cells at an early embryonic stage.
items.knowledgeNote: Because the corrected cells do not divide indefinitely, gene therapy here is a treatment, not a cure — a standard examiner's follow-up question.

items.subject: chemistry
items.question: What is the aldol condensation? Write the reaction of acetaldehyde with dilute NaOH and state the product.
items.reference:
**Aldol condensation:** an aldehyde or ketone with at least one α-hydrogen forms a carbanion (enolate) in dilute base; this attacks the carbonyl carbon of a second molecule, giving a β-hydroxy aldehyde (aldol). On heating, aldol loses water to give an α,β-unsaturated carbonyl.

For acetaldehyde: CH₃CHO + CH₃CHO → **CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CHO (aldol)** → on heating, **CH₃CH=CHCHO (crotonaldehyde)**.
items.knowledgeNote: No α-hydrogen → no aldol: benzaldehyde (no α-H) instead undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction with conc. NaOH, giving benzyl alcohol and benzoate.

items.subject: english
items.question: Write, in about 120 words, a summary of the passage in the first question.
items.reference: The passage argues that forests are undervalued because markets count only the timber they yield. Their real worth lies in preventing landslides, recharging springs, supporting pollinators and storing carbon — benefits a cleared slope destroys forever. Nepal's community forestry shows the remedy: when local people manage the forest beside them, they protect it, whereas an outside contractor takes what can be sold and leaves. The lesson is that sustainable management depends on the people who bear the consequences, not on distant profit.
items.knowledgeNote: A summary keeps the central argument and order, drops examples and repetition, and stays within the word limit — do not add opinions.

items.subject: mathematics
items.question: If y = √(1 + x²), prove that (1 + x²)y″ + x y′ = y.
items.reference:
y² = 1 + x², so differentiating: 2y y′ = 2x → y′ = x/y.

Differentiate again: y″ = (y·1 − x·y′)/y² = (y − x·(x/y))/y² = (y² − x²)/y³.

Since y² − x² = 1, we get y″ = 1/y³.

Now (1 + x²)y″ + x y′ = y²·(1/y³) + x·(x/y) = 1/y + x²/y = (1 + x²)/y = y²/y = **y**, as required.
items.knowledgeNote: This style of proof (square first, differentiate implicitly) avoids ugly square roots in the second derivative — always look for it.

items.subject: nepali
items.question: विद्यालयको नाममा पुस्तकालयको समय विस्तार गर्ने सम्बन्धी आधिकारिक पत्र लेख्नुहोस्।
items.reference:
श्रीमान् प्रधानाध्यापकज्यू,
श्री जनज्योति माध्यमिक विद्यालय,
सिन्धुपाल्चोक।

विषय: पुस्तकालयको समय विस्तारबारे।

महोदय,

हाम्रो विद्यालयको पुस्तकालय हाल बिहान १० बजेदेखि दिउँसो ३ बजेसम्म खुल्ने गर्छ। तर वार्षिक परीक्षा नजिकिँदै गर्दा विद्यार्थीलाई सन्दर्भ पुस्तक हेर्न र समूह अध्ययन गर्न समय अपुग भइरहेको छ।

यसैले परीक्षाको अवधिभर पुस्तकालय साँझ ५ बजेसम्म खुला राख्न, एकजना सहायक पुस्तकपाल नियुक्त गर्न र विद्यार्थी परिचयपत्रका आधारमा पुस्तक लिएर पढ्न दिने व्यवस्था मिलाइदिनुहुन हार्दिक अनुरोध गर्दछु।

भवदीय,
विद्यार्थी प्रतिनिधि
कक्षा १२, ख
